about: Generic FDM and fastener rules for --mode assembly. No number here is specific to any request or enclosure: request numbers come from the request/L1 text and part numbers from benchmarks/enclosure/parts/*/part.json. Every value carries its source. Values used in a design are recorded with provenance 'rules:<key>'. This file is reviewed by hand (test_no_hardcoding does not scan JSON).

sliding_fit_min.source: FDM practice: minimum per-side clearance for a sliding fit with a 0.4 mm nozzle (requirements.md A11)

sliding_fit_max.source: FDM practice: maximum per-side clearance before a fit rattles (requirements.md A11)

board_to_wall.source: default clearance between a board edge and a printed wall when the request is silent (requirements.md A11)

plug_to_opening.source: clearance between a cable plug envelope and its wall opening (FDM hole shrinkage plus plug tolerance)

opening_oversize_max.source: default maximum opening oversize beyond the plug envelope when the request is silent

min_ligament.source: minimum printed material between an opening and an edge or another opening (about 4 perimeters at 0.4 mm)

overhang_angle_deg.source: FDM practice: steepest unsupported overhang measured from vertical

bridge_max.source: FDM practice: longest reliable bridge in PLA/PETG

round_hole_exempt_max.source: FDM practice: round holes in vertical walls up to this diameter print without support

fn.source: $fn for round features, same as cad_agent.SEGMENTS

standoff_wall_min.source: printed material around a pilot hole (4 perimeters)

component_height_default.source: keep-out above a populated board when the request gives no height: tallest common through-hole parts (electrolytics, trimmers) - used only when the request is silent, flagged as an assumption

solder_side_default.source: solder fillets plus clipped leads below a through-hole board - used only when the request is silent, flagged as an assumption

keepout_margin.source: margin added to an estimated keep-out height

plug_travel.source: length a cable plug envelope is swept outward past its overmold so it runs 'past any wall' (several wall thicknesses plus a hand gripping the plug)

driver_clearance.source: radial room around a pan screw head for the driver bit and its wobble (seat column = head diameter + 2 x this)

driver_diameter.source: shaft of a common #1 Phillips / 2.5 mm hex screwdriver plus wobble

driver_reach.source: screwdriver shaft length above the base rim with the lid off: V-DRIVER runs from the board top to the rim plus this (requirements.md V-DRIVER); a generic tool length

design_margin.source: setpoint offset inside one-sided clearance limits: 5 x the judge's 0.02 mm measurement epsilon (rubric.md 3.2), so tessellation and rounding never flip a pass; derivation targets only, checks keep their limits (ARCHITECTURE.md 7.7)

grid_search_step.source: coarse step of the grid-feasibility search over one pitch cell (ARCHITECTURE.md 7.9): a measurement resolution 1/15 of grid_residual_max and the judge's 0.01 mm reporting precision; each result is refined locally below 1e-9 mm

grid_residual_max.source: a 0.64 mm square pin in a ~1.0 mm plated hole: lateral slack before the pin no longer drops into the grid hole (requirements.md A7)

overlap_max.source: largest overlap of two printed bodies in the closed pose that is still numerical contact, not interpenetration (requirements.md L3.7.1.2; cad_checks.OVERLAP_VOLUME)

interference_max.source: largest intersection of two reference parts counted as touching (requirements.md R7)

seat_gap_max.source: largest gap between a board's underside and a standoff top for the board to count as seated (requirements.md seating rule)

seat_axis_residual_max.source: largest board-hole to pilot-axis offset for a screw to start straight (requirements.md seating rule)

lip_engagement.source: FDM practice: height a locating lid lip overlaps the base wall (about 10 layers)

lip_wall.source: three 0.4 mm perimeters: the thinnest lip that prints stiff

boss_wall_min.source: printed material around a lid-screw pilot (4 perimeters), same as standoff_wall_min

cut_overrun.source: a cut runs this far past each face it must clear, so no zero-thickness skin is left

screw_hole_clearance_min.source: ISO 273 medium series: radial clearance of a screw through a hole (M2.5 -> 2.9, M3 -> 3.4)

given_hole_clearance_min.source: radial clearance a screw needs through a board's existing mounting hole: the hole is a fixed datum, so a screw passes it when its major diameter fits (requirements.md A9: 'M2 passes the 2.0 holes'); ISO 273 clearance (screw_hole_clearance_min) applies only to holes the design makes

max_quantity.source: largest quantity of one catalogue part offered to the controller per request

part_to_wall.source: smallest gap between a placed module (with its headers) and a printed surface: FDM dimensional tolerance plus assembly slop

measure_tol.source: measurement tolerance of the agent's own checks: half the judge's 0.02 mm (rubric.md 3.2), so the agent is the stricter of the two

margin_scale.source: normalisation length of check margins (margin 1.0 = 1 mm of slack)

lookup_k.source: catalogue candidates offered per part kind

view_elevation_deg.source: camera elevation above horizontal for the elevation renders of assembly mode, so openings show

arrange_rank_max.source: generic cap on controller-ranked layout candidates (feasible edge assignments ConfirmArrangement scores); reported in design.json when it truncates

layout_step.source: step of the 1-D shift search that resolves a placement collision

aperture_min_volume.source: aperture regions smaller than this are numerical slivers, not openings (rubric.md 3.4)

parity_volume_rel.source: OpenSCAD vs manifold3d volume agreement for the delivered mesh (ARCHITECTURE.md 3.2)

parity_bbox.source: OpenSCAD vs manifold3d bounding-box agreement for the delivered mesh (ARCHITECTURE.md 3.2)

rebate_upstand.source: generalize delta 003 C2: the wall left outside a lid rebate, 4 perimeters at 0.4 mm (the same printed-ligament basis as min_ligament)

vent_slot_width.source: generalize delta 003 C3: vent slot width when the text gives no width band, 5 extrusion lines at 0.4 mm; flagged as an assumption when used

vent_slot_length.source: generalize delta 003 C3: vent slot length in a lid row when the text gives no length band (common FDM vent practice, 8-12 mm); flagged as an assumption when used

controller_step_budget.source: migration delta R01 (owner decision D1): the closed-loop controller's correction steps per run. A step is one voted question (3 samples) plus the re-run of the stages its action invalidates and one manifold build (seconds; an arrangement re-run asks its own questions), so 6 steps stay far inside the 20-minute run timeout and cover one correction per named mating connector of the largest train contents (4) plus a structural correction and a spare

controller_trust_region.source: migration delta R01: a step that keeps the number of failing checks may raise their summed normalised violation by at most this much (half of design_margin) and still be kept; a step that adds a failing check is always undone

controller_error_terms.source: migration delta R01: failing checks shown to the controller per step, ranked actionable first then worst margin; a 9B model answers short enum questions best (benchmarks/reports/2026-10-23-voting.md)

controller_menu_max.source: migration delta R01: actions offered per step (plus stop); a short menu keeps the question a discrete choice (content-keyed since R02)

menu_orderings.source: migration delta R02: every discrete LLM menu question is asked under this many seeded orderings of its options (permutation voting, menus.py); 3 keeps the call count of R01's 3-sample vote (benchmarks/generalize/loop/iter_R02/audit_before.json: the 9B picked the first lettered option in 11 of 12 logged menus but the first shuffled one in 36%, about chance, so order must vary between samples to be measured)

menu_samples.source: migration delta R02: samples per ordering (the first greedy, later ones at temperature 0.7); 1 x 3 orderings = R01's 3 calls per question

menu_consistency_min.source: migration delta R02: a menu choice is high-confidence only when this share of its valid answers across orderings agrees with the winner (1.0 = every ordering); below it the closed loop measures the alternatives instead of trusting the vote (Zheng et al. ICLR 2024; small-model verbalized confidence is near-constant, so agreement across permutations is the confidence signal)

menu_min_valid.source: migration delta R02: valid answers needed before a menu choice can be high-confidence (one answer measures no consistency)

controller_search_k.source: migration delta R02: verifier-guided best-of-N: at most this many surviving actions per controller step are applied on forks and measured (every voted action, plus the next-ranked ones when the vote is inconsistent); the R01 train menus held 2-4 entries, so 3 covers them

controller_search_depth.source: migration delta R02: lookahead steps per candidate (1 = best-of-N on the immediate measured error; deeper beam lookahead is not implemented yet and is clipped to 1)

controller_search_max_evals.source: migration delta R02: plant evaluations (fork, re-run, manifold build) the closed loop may spend per run, a hard cap (R02/R11 review fix 2: once spent the loop stops before asking; no step measures beyond it); 12 = step budget 6 x 2, a few seconds each, far inside the run timeout

support_ledge_width.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): the strip of a part's underside a printed ledge carries, inside the part's edge (three 0.4 mm lines)

support_min_length.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): the shortest ledge, rim or rib segment the plant prints (shorter pieces break off; about four min_feature widths)

retention_wall.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): wall of a locating rim round a part (three 0.4 mm perimeters, as lip_wall)

pocket_rim_height.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): the highest a locating rim rises above the part's seat; it never rises above the part's top plane

retention_play_max.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): the farthest a held part may move in any direction before it rattles (twice the middle of the sliding-fit band)

crush_rib_width.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): width of a vertical crush rib along the part's edge (two to three 0.4 mm lines)

crush_rib_pitch.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): one crush rib per this much free rim length, at least one per rim segment

crush_rib_interference.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): how far a crush rib reaches into the part outline (FDM crush-rib practice 0.1 to 0.3 mm; the rib deforms on insertion)

crush_rib_interference_min.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): below this a crush rib does not grip (within FDM dimensional scatter)

crush_rib_interference_max.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): above this a crush rib cracks or the part will not go in (FDM crush-rib practice)

snap_arm_thickness.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): thickness of a printed cantilever snap arm in its bending direction (about four perimeters)

snap_clip_width.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): width of a cantilever snap arm along the part's edge

snap_overlap.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): how far a snap hook reaches over the part's top face (snap-fit design guides: about half to one millimetre for small printed hooks)

snap_overlap_min.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): a hook that overlaps less releases under handling loads

snap_hook_height.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): height of a snap hook's head above the part's top face

snap_gap.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): vertical play between a part's top face and the underside of the snap hook (FDM layer scatter)

snap_slot.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): gap that frees a snap arm from the rim beside it so it can flex

snap_strain_max.source: migration delta R11 (cradle): permissible bending strain of a printed PLA/PETG cantilever snap arm, used repeatedly (snap-fit design guides give 1.5-3 percent for brittle thermoplastics; strain = 1.5 t y / L^2)

plate_wall_min.source: migration delta R12 (plate): printed material kept round every cut of a load-carrying plate (slots, nut channels, recesses, stud holes) and to its outline; FDM practice for a bolted printed part, 7 to 8 perimeters at 0.4 mm (assumption, uncertainty +/-1 mm)

plate_floor_min.source: migration delta R12 (plate): printed floor between a part's bolted face and the nut a bolt clamps through it (10 layers of 0.2 mm), so the preload does not crush it (assumption, uncertainty +/-1 mm)

bolt_tip_cover.source: migration delta R12 (plate): a bolt tip stays at least this far below the plate face it must not reach (a protruding tip catches whatever touches the face; assumption)

nut_trap_clearance_min.source: migration delta R12 (plate): smallest clearance per flat side of a printed hex nut trap that still takes the nut (FDM practice; catalogue nuts give their own nominal trap_clearance)

nut_trap_clearance_max.source: migration delta R12 (plate): largest clearance per flat side at which a printed hex trap still stops the nut turning (FDM practice; the trap must stay narrower than the nut's corners)

grip_pin_diameter.source: migration delta R12 (surface features): diameter of a printed traction pin (5 extrusion widths; assumption, uncertainty +/-1 mm)

grip_count_default.source: migration delta R12 (surface features): raised features placed when the text states no count (assumption: a few features at each corner and between them; uncertainty +/-4)

grip_height_default.source: migration delta R12 (surface features): protrusion of a raised feature when the text states no height (assumption: a few millimetres stand clear of a flat face without catching; uncertainty +/-1 mm)

grip_edge_default.source: migration delta R12 (surface features): smallest distance of a raised feature from the face's edge when the text states none (assumption)

sweep_step_deg.source: migration delta R12: angular step of a swept keep-out (a keep-out rotating about a datum through a catalogue angle); at 80 mm radius the chord error is under 0.02 mm, the judge's measurement epsilon

position_step.source: migration delta R12 (plate): grid step of the plate outline position search that clears the reference keep-outs

tapped_engagement_ratio.source: migration delta R12 (plate): a screw threaded into a part's tapped metal hole engages at least this many thread diameters (machine-design practice: 1 x d in steel or aluminium; the part's own thread depth caps it)

stress_sizing_iterations.source: migration delta R12 (plate): most re-sizing passes of the plate thickness against a stated bending load (each pass measures the built section)

stress_tol.source: review fix R12 N7: tolerance of the load_stress check on the allowed bending stress (the section of a faceted mesh moves the measured stress by about 0.3 percent at 16 MPa); was a hard-coded 0.1 MPa

clamp_bearing_ratio_min.source: review fix R12 B1 (ASSUMPTION, bolted-joint practice): smallest share of a fastener's nominal bearing face (nut flats or head, less its bolt clearance hole) that must rest on printed material, with the bolt axis inside the bearing's convex hull; a hex nut over a slot of its bolt's clearance width keeps its two side lands, about 40 percent of its face for ISO metric nuts (hand calculation in test_plate), and below 30 percent or with the lands on one side the nut tips or pulls through under preload (uncertainty +/-10 percent)

thin_probe_step.source: review fix R12 N5: spacing of the sections the thin_feature sensor cuts along x, y and z (a thin wall is long in at least one direction, so sections across it find it)

plastic_thread_engagement_ratio.source: review fix R12 (stud engagement sensor): a screw tapped into printed plastic engages at least this many thread diameters (FDM practice 1.5 to 2 x d; the catalogue's own min_engagement may ask more)

stress_probe_step.source: R12 review 2 (N1): spacing of the load-case positions the load_stress sensor and the load sizing evaluate: the patch centre along each outline edge (both corners always included) and the bolted part's shift over its adjustment range (both extremes and the middle always included)

fastener_preload_stress_default.source: R12 review 2 (N4), ASSUMPTION: the preload of a bolt clamping printed parts when the text states none, as a stress on the thread's core (tap drill) area: about 10 percent of an ISO 8.8 assembly preload (~600-700 MPa on the stress area), a hand-tight joint into printed material (M5: ~970 N, M3: ~340 N; uncertainty x2)

print_strength_default.source: R12 review 2 (N4), ASSUMPTION: the in-plane strength of the printed material when the text states none (PETG / PLA FDM parts across layers, 20-40 MPa; the lower end)

shear_strength_ratio.source: R12 review 2 (N4): the shear strength of the printed material as a share of its stated strength (Tresca; punch-through of a floor round a nut or a head is a shear failure)

bearing_strength_ratio.source: R12 review 2 (N4), ASSUMPTION: the bearing (compressive contact) pressure the printed material carries under a nut or a head as a share of its stated strength (conservative: printed PETG / PLA compressive strength is about 1 to 1.5 times its tensile strength)

spec_slots.about: Generic enclosure spec slots. The controller maps each slot onto one number occurrence that Python extracted from the request or L1 text (or 'none'); a 'none' slot takes its default_rule value and is flagged as an assumption. A slot whose default_rule is null must come from the text unless it says "required": false (the board size slots: a primary reference that is not request-sized needs no number, and a request-sized one takes its size from them when they are filled, else from the part-size question; generalize delta 001 D4). The required flag is never shown to the controller.

slots.name: board_width
slots.meaning: the length of the circuit board's longer edge

slots.name: board_depth
slots.meaning: the length of the circuit board's shorter edge

slots.name: keepout_above
slots.meaning: the free height that must stay clear above the board's top surface (component keep-out)

slots.name: keepout_below
slots.meaning: the free height that must stay clear below the board's underside (solder side)

slots.name: board_clearance
slots.meaning: the minimum gap between the board and any printed surface

slots.name: headroom
slots.meaning: the minimum free space required above the tallest part on the board

slots.name: opening_oversize_max
slots.meaning: the most a wall opening may be bigger than its cable plug, per side

slots.name: wall_min
slots.meaning: the minimum wall, floor and lid thickness

slots.name: wall_max
slots.meaning: the maximum wall, floor and lid thickness

slots.name: max_x
slots.meaning: the largest allowed outside length of the closed enclosure (its longest side)

slots.name: max_y
slots.meaning: the largest allowed outside width of the closed enclosure

slots.name: max_z
slots.meaning: the largest allowed outside height of the closed enclosure

forms.about: Migration delta R12: the spec slots of each non-shell archetype (structural form). ParseSpec asks the shell slots above always (unchanged, so the enclosure regression parses as before) and adds a form's slots when a part the text names can anchor that form (catalogue data: a bolt_face interface for the plate). Every slot is optional (no default: a silent slot sets no limit and no sensor). `range` is the plausible band Python checks a mapped number against; `pair`/`side` tie a lo/hi band; `sets` (R12 review 2, N6) makes a slot one stated value that sets both ends of a band (Python copies it to each end the text left unmapped: slot semantics, no text rule); the unit is checked against the word after the number (unit_words).

plate.name: size_min
plate.meaning: the smallest allowed plan length of the printed plate or platform along each of its sides

plate.name: size_max
plate.meaning: the largest allowed plan length of the printed plate or platform along each of its sides

plate.name: thickness_min
plate.meaning: the smallest allowed thickness of the printed plate or platform (not counting raised features)

plate.name: thickness_max
plate.meaning: the largest allowed thickness of the printed plate or platform (not counting raised features)

plate.name: size_exact
plate.meaning: the plan length of the printed plate or platform along each of its sides, when the text states one value and not a range

plate.name: thickness_exact
plate.meaning: the thickness of the printed plate or platform (not counting raised features), when the text states one value and not a range

plate.name: ref_clearance
plate.meaning: the smallest gap the printed part must keep from a neighbouring part or its keep-out zone

plate.name: load_force
plate.meaning: the force of the load case the printed part must carry

plate.name: load_patch
plate.meaning: the side length of the square patch the load case acts on

plate.name: strength
plate.meaning: the strength of the printed material used for the load case

plate.name: safety_factor
plate.meaning: the safety factor the load case stress must keep below the material strength

plate.name: bearing_area_min
plate.meaning: the smallest flat area the printed part must bear on

plate.name: feature_count_min
plate.meaning: the fewest raised grip features (pins, studs or ridges) on the face

plate.name: feature_height_min
plate.meaning: the smallest height of each raised grip feature

plate.name: feature_height_max
plate.meaning: the largest height of each raised grip feature

plate.name: feature_edge_min
plate.meaning: the smallest distance of the raised grip features from the edge of the face

plate.name: feature_coverage_min
plate.meaning: the smallest share of the face's plan area the raised grip features must spread over

plate.name: adjust_min
plate.meaning: the smallest adjustment range of a bolted part's position along its main adjustment direction

plate.name: adjust_cross_min
plate.meaning: the smallest adjustment range of a bolted part's position across its main adjustment direction

plate.name: feature_min
plate.meaning: the thinnest printed feature or wall allowed anywhere in the printed part

plate.name: fastener_preload
plate.meaning: the clamping force (preload) of each bolt or screw that fastens a part to the printed part

unit_words.about: Migration delta R12, review fix N2: the words that state a unit right after a number in the text (lower case), each with its scale factor to the unit (a prefixed unit is the word with its factor: 2.5 kN states 2500 N). ParseSpec scales a mapped number by its word's factor and rejects a mapping whose number carries a word of another unit than the slot's (a number with no unit word is accepted unscaled: the text does not say). The regex units mm / cm / deg of extract_numbers are already scaled there (their factor here is not applied twice).
unit_words.source: SI prefixes and common engineering units (1 psi = 0.00689476 MPa, 1 ksi = 6.89476 MPa)

trace_names.about: R12 review 2 (N7): the deterministic L1 trace (assembly.trace_links) for checks that measure a generic property of the printed part rather than a catalogue part or a mapped number: a check of this type also links every L1 that names one of these words (token runs, as catalogue `names`). Trace only: it never decides geometry, a choice or a pass; a check's own measurement decides PASS / FAIL.
trace_names.source: the vocabulary of FDM printing and bolted joints

archetypes.about: The archetypes (structural forms) the derivation rules can build. Since migration delta R12 an archetype is feasible when its `needs` hold in the catalogue data (plant feasibility, forms.py) and the controller chooses among the feasible ones (a content-keyed, permutation-voted menu, then set_archetype in the closed loop); the `evidence` words are only the form_evidence sensor's vocabulary (a text naming another buildable form's words and none of the current one's is reported, never decided). Until R12 they were a gate (generalize delta 001 D5). `meaning` is the controller's gloss. Generic vocabulary only; no design names. housing and block are left out on purpose: they name bearing housings and pillow blocks (block archetype, GM5).

tray_lid.meaning: an enclosure: a printed tray and lid closed round the contents, which are held inside on standoffs or in a cradle
tray_lid.source: words that ask for a body enclosing its contents; a generic vocabulary, no design names. lid_words (generalize delta 003 C2): the evidence words that name the lid, so a closure word gates only in a sentence about the lid

plate.needs: a content part with a bolt_face interface
plate.meaning: a flat printed plate or platform that the parts bolt to face-on (bolts through slots or holes into captive nuts, or screws into tapped parts), keeping clear of the parts it sits on or next to
plate.source: migration delta R12: words that ask for a flat body parts are bolted to; a generic vocabulary, no design names (form_evidence sensor only, never a gate)

closures.about: How the lid of a tray_lid closes on the base (generalize delta 003 C2). The default closure is used unless one sentence of the request or an L1 names a closure's evidence word and a lid word (archetypes.tray_lid.lid_words; text_evidence token runs). The form is a rule: no controller question. Generic vocabulary only.

lip.meaning: a lid plate over the walls with a locating lip that drops inside them

rebate.meaning: a flat plate that drops into a rebate in the top of the walls, flush with the upstand
rebate.source: English / joinery: a rebate is a step cut along an edge to receive a panel

vents.about: Vent slot rows (generalize delta 003 C3). A vent sentence is a sentence of the request or an L1 that contains one of the evidence words (text_evidence token runs). Bare 'exhaust' (a fan's exhaust side) and bare 'slot' (a card slot) are not evidence. The slots are the generated spec slots of the one voted size question (assy_vent_spec), each with a meaning and a unit; a silent slot is none, and rules.vent_slot_width / vent_slot_length fill a silent width or lid-row length.
vents.source: English words for openings that let air through a wall or lid; a generic vocabulary, no design names

slots.name: vent_count_min
slots.meaning: the fewest vent slots the row may have

slots.name: vent_count_max
slots.meaning: the most vent slots the row may have

slots.name: vent_width_min
slots.meaning: the smallest width of one vent slot (its narrow side)

slots.name: vent_width_max
slots.meaning: the largest width of one vent slot (its narrow side)

slots.name: vent_length_min
slots.meaning: the smallest length (or height) of one vent slot (its long side)

slots.name: vent_length_max
slots.meaning: the largest length (or height) of one vent slot (its long side)

slots.name: vent_pitch_min
slots.meaning: the smallest centre-to-centre spacing of neighbouring vent slots

slots.name: vent_pitch_max
slots.meaning: the largest centre-to-centre spacing of neighbouring vent slots

slots.name: vent_area_min
slots.meaning: the smallest total open area of all vent slots together

face_relations.about: How a text relates the walls two exposed cable connectors face (generalize delta 002 C0). A pair of exposed connectors may take a relation only when one sentence of the request or an L1 names both parts (their part.json names) and one of the relation's evidence words (text_evidence token runs); the controller then reads the relation from the request (one voted enum per gated pair, plus not_stated) and a unanimous reading becomes a face_relation check. Generic English relation words only; no design names or numbers.

same.meaning: both connectors open through the same end or side of the enclosure
same.wall_meaning: the same wall that connector opens through

opposite.meaning: the two connectors open through opposite ends or sides of the enclosure
opposite.wall_meaning: the wall opposite the one that connector opens through

fastener_roles.about: Words that say a fastener named in the same clause of the request or an L1 holds the primary board (generalize delta 002 C1): the board screw is the largest such named catalogue screw that passes the board's holes, else the thread the board's mount_holes interface declares, else the smallest screw that passes. The primary's own part.json names count as role evidence too. Generic vocabulary only.

board.source: words a requirement uses for the part held on standoffs at its mounting holes

building_blocks.about: Migration delta R11: generic building blocks the controller selects among (Python enumerates the options the plant can build for the design, sizes them from part data and the rules above, and sensors measure them). No design names.

retention.about: How a part without mounting holes (no mount_holes interface; it rests on its seat plane) is held in a shell: a cradle of ledges under its edges and a locating rim round it, plus the option's retention feature. The default is the plant's proposal; the retention sensor reports the part's free travel, and the controller may choose another option with set_retention.

pocket.meaning: a locating pocket: ledges under the part's edges and a rim round it with a sliding fit; nothing holds it down
pocket.source: plant default (reads no text): the minimal cradle

crush_ribs.meaning: the pocket with vertical crush ribs on the rim that press on the part's edges, so friction holds it in every direction
crush_ribs.source: FDM practice: crush ribs give a press fit that tolerates print scatter

snap_clips.meaning: the pocket with two cantilever snap clips whose hooks reach over the part's top face at opposite edges

surface_feature.about: Migration delta R12: raised features on a plate's free face (traction or locating features). The default is none (the plant adds nothing on its own); the surface_features sensor reports a count, height, edge distance or spread the text's mapped numbers ask for, and the controller adds a feature kind with add_surface_feature. Python lays the features out and sizes them within the mapped bands.

none.meaning: a plain face with no raised features

studs.meaning: threaded catalogue set screws in tapped holes, standing proud of the face as studs (not printed, so the face can print flat on the bed)
studs.source: mechanical practice: replaceable steel studs are set screws in tapped holes

pins.meaning: printed cylindrical pins standing on the face (printed with the plate, so that face must print facing up)

nut_retention.about: Migration delta R12: how a plate holds the nuts of a bolt-through chain. The default is the plant's proposal (reads no text); the travel sensors report each declared adjustment axis the bolts cannot move along, and the controller may choose another option with set_nut_retention. A hex trap stops a nut turning only while it slides along one direction, so a part adjustable along two directions needs the frame.

channel.meaning: hex nut channels in the plate, open to its free face, along the largest adjustment range (the nuts slide one way only)
channel.source: plant default (reads no text): FDM practice, captive hex nut channels

frame.meaning: a separate printed nut frame holding every nut in a hex trap on its own floor, sliding in a pocket of the plate that covers the adjustment in every declared direction, wide enough to bear on the plate beside the bolt slots
frame.source: bolted-joint practice: a floating nut carrier (a nut plate) slides in a pocket so a fastened part can be set along two directions; a carrier holding two nuts cannot turn in a pocket narrower than its diagonal

handedness.about: Migration delta R12: when a reference part the design attaches to is used in left/right mirror pairs (part.json mirror_pair), the design either serves both with one part (its mirror image passes too) or is delivered as a declared mirror pair. The default is one part; the handedness sensor measures the mirror image, and the controller may declare a pair with set_handedness.

single.meaning: one printed part serves both sides (it must pass on the mirrored reference too)

mirror_pair.meaning: a declared left/right pair: the part and its mirror image, each for its own side
mirror_pair.source: mechanical practice: handed parts are made as mirror pairs

base.source: a tray prints on its floor without support

lid.source: a lid prints on its flat outer face; the lip points up
